topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Mutation-driven cancer development and susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations accumulate and enable cancer development within a susceptible cell and permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposure to cancer risk against explanations based on chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and cellular mutations.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why mutational initiation may require subsequent tumour-promoting conditions for cancer to develop.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and the synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics place tissue-specific susceptibility within the broader explanation of how carcinogenic mechanisms produce cancer.

topics.label: Evidence linking human cancers to carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how evidence from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how experimental assays test carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
